units.spine: A stranger arriving in Hochhausen finds the market without asking the way, because the town's own road leads there on its own.
A traveller passing through Hochhausen finds armed order already in place, professionals kept on for the town's safety rather than left to chance.
In Hochhausen, people find plenty to argue about besides money.
Hochhausen is a town that works: it gets what it needs and moves what it makes.
What Hochhausen could hold, it could not hold for long.
The town could hold against what it expects, and everyone here knows it could not against what it does not.
Nothing in Hochhausen stands organised against what lives beyond the fields, and each household answers for its own fences.
More disagreements stay open in Hochhausen than get closed.
A careful eye passing through Hochhausen notices first that there is nothing spare in it.
No practitioner of magic is kept in Hochhausen, no arrangement for one, and no expectation of either.
Food security in Hochhausen rests on its own harvest, safe from a closed road and not from a bad year.
A day spent in Hochhausen would not be enough to learn that The Commercial Circle and The Administrative Circle are at odds. It shows itself only on a longer stay.
Goods move into Hochhausen and out of it, and neither direction draws a second look.
Set on a road, Hochhausen lives by it: goods in, goods out, people passing through.
Settled at the size a place of its kind settles at, the town has not grown past that mark.
One tie in Hochhausen outweighs the rest, and it shows in what the town does and does not do.
The people of Hochhausen are connected the way people in any settled place are, with no single tie among them that stands out from the rest.
One loose end shows itself on a close look at Hochhausen, the kind a single institution would tie off.
